purpose: Sensitivity of the two-phase method to uncertain treatment consumption and protection-band width
controls: Same accepted CNN, 15-day CA forecast, weather, initial fire, asset cores, management polygons, eligibility, program costs and search settings. No model refitting or benchmark reruns.
bounds: Recompute each asset-plus-band bound from the strongest whole-polygon treatment reference under that scenario. No percentage slack. Numerical tolerance stays 1e-8 ha.
interpretation: Deterministic scenario sensitivity. The alternatives are transferred literature values, not confidence limits or a calibration of the learned fuel coefficient. Coarse dead and live woody loads stay unchanged in the grass cases to isolate uncertainty in the components assumed completely consumed.

scenarios.name: grass_high_consumption
scenarios.description: Consume 95% of herbaceous and 100% of one-hour dead load in GR classes.

scenarios.name: grass_low_consumption
scenarios.description: Consume 80% of herbaceous and 90% of one-hour dead load in GR classes.

scenarios.name: shrub_residual_017
scenarios.description: Transfer the 83% consumption measured at the ceanothus site to the existing GS/SH treatment cells.

scenarios.name: shrub_residual_050
scenarios.description: Test 50% remaining biomass, motivated by the description of retained green chaparral biomass on north exposures. This is a broader transfer scenario, not a measured Pier response.

scenarios.name: band_100m
scenarios.description: Use 100 m around the same asset cores, with nominal treatment responses.

scenarios.name: band_200m
scenarios.description: Use 200 m around the same asset cores, with nominal treatment responses.

carb2025.title: California Wildfire & Prescribed Fire Emission Inventory: Updates to Methodology & Data Sources
carb2025.location: Slide 62 (PDF page 63), Broadcast Burn: Consumption Assumptions
carb2025.supports: Inventory assumptions at fuel moistures 12 to 16%: herbaceous consumption 80 to 95%, one-hour fuel consumption 90 to 100%. These are inventory assumptions, not a field-estimated uncertainty distribution.

hardy1996.supports: Consumed biomass fractions 0.75 to 0.83 across standing chaparral sites. The 0.83 site was dominated by ceanothus. Site means do not establish species-specific responses for Pier.

green1982.supports: Unburned green fuel may comprise half or more of chaparral biomass on north exposures. This motivates a 0.5 scenario, not a confidence bound.
